https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/09/0.text: By Ned Garvey Sep. 8, 2026 Supporters of Germany's Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) party demonstrate in support of the Russian House in Berlin. REUTERS / Liesa Johannssen BERLIN — On a rainy Friday evening in Germany’s capital, hundreds of people gathered to protest the government’s announcement that it was terminating the lease of the Russian House, a Russian cultural center owned and operated by Moscow. Demonstrators called on the government to reverse its decision, end its “russophobia” and stop what they called its constant “aggression” toward Russia. “It’s the only place left for cultural exchange,” a protester told The Moscow Times, declining to give their name. Down the street, a dozen or so supporters of Russia’s liberal opposition chanted slogans like “Russia without Putin” and held signs up with phrases like “The Kremlin shouldn’t have an address in Berlin.” A bit further away, roughly 100 pro-Ukraine activists held up boxes that symbolized suitcases and bore slogans like “Suitcase, train station, Moscow,” and spoke about their efforts to close the Russian House dating back to 2022. Supporters of Russia’s liberal opposition rally in support of the closure of Berlin's Russian House. Ned Garvey The flurry of demonstrations came after Germany said it would shutter the Russian House after it officially blamed Moscow for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in early August. But closing it, or the bookstore on its premises — places many demonstrators viewed as places of cultural enrichment — may not prove as simple or straightforward as the government’s announcement made it seem. Several protesters told The Moscow Times that the decision to close the Russian House was politically motivated and “regrettable.” Shortly after Berlin announced its closure, the Russian government said that it would move to shut down Germany's Goethe-Institut cultural centers — a decision many demonstrators told The Moscow Times was a “different matter.” What is the Russian House? Located in Berlin-Mitte, what is now the Russian House opened in East Berlin in 1984 as the House of Soviet Science and Culture, and only later became the Russian House after the Soviet collapse. The seven-story, 30,000-square-meter building has been the subject of fierce debate since at least the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The House of Soviet Science and Culture (the present-day Russian House) in Berlin in 1984. wikimapia.org According to its website, the Russian House aims to “familiarize German visitors with important aspects and events in Russian culture and science,” as well as to support Russians in Germany “in preserving and developing their national and cultural identity.” Organizers say the institution attracts around 200,000 visitors per year to its programming of Russian language courses, film screenings, cultural events, concerts and more. In July, Director Pavel Izvolskiy told the newspaper nd that the Russian House’s mission was to build bridges between Germans and Russians, a mission it has followed since 1984. It is operated and owned by Rossotrudnichestvo, the Russian government agency responsible for cultural exchange and foreign aid. The European Union sanctioned Rossotrudnichestvo in 2022, calling it “the main state agency projecting the Kremlin’s soft power and hybrid influence, including the promotion of the so-called ‘Russkiy Mir’ concept,” and accusing it of organizing “international events aimed at consolidating a wider public perception of the occupied Ukrainian territories as Russian.” Izvolskiy told nd that Rossotrudnichestvo is not the center’s operator, but “merely ensures” its operation. But in June 2025, a Munich administrative court ruled that the Russian House was indeed subject to the sanctions placed on Rossotrudnichestvo, meaning that it would only be able to disburse funds for "maintenance operations.” Its German bank account was frozen, meaning all bank transactions must be approved by the German Bundesbank. Can Germany even close the Russian House? After the announcement was made, German media pointed out that closing the Russian House would not be as simple as the government made it seem. Firstly, it is governed by a 2011-2012 intergovernmental treaty on cultural information centers. That treaty is automatically renewed unless terminated, with the current version ending on June 7, 2027. According to the Frankfurter Allgemeine newspaper, the German government has until Dec. 6 to cancel the agreement. Activists protest under the slogan "No Kremlin in Berlin" against a demonstration by Germany's Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) party in support of the Russian House. REUTERS / Liesa Johannssen Furthermore, the building remains the property of the Russian Federation. While the land belongs to Germany, the two governments signed a 2013 agreement which granted Russia its use for 99 years. The Russian Embassy in Berlin wrote on X last week that the German government had ordered all Russian staff of the Russian House and the Russian consulate in Bonn to leave the country “as quickly as possible.” However, a source connected to the Russian House told The Moscow Times that there “aren’t actually that many staff members who had moved there [solely for work],” and that many of the staff members have European passports. Propaganda and espionage One of the main controversies surrounding the Russian House stems from its 2022 screening of a documentary about the murder of Jews in Belarus which allegedly depicted Ukrainians as Nazis. Another charge leveled at the Russian House is that the bookstore inside its premises sold bars of soap in the shape of Russian tanks. “It's time we recognized that this isn't about mutual cultural exchange, but rather Russian war propaganda in Germany,” Green Party MP Robin Wagener, the politician who made that claim, told Deutsche Welle. Moreover, France in July accused the Russian House of espionage, saying it was “used as a cover by Russian intelligence services.” “Its energy consumption is significantly higher than what you would expect from a cultural institution,” said Roderich Kiesewetter, a German MP from the center-right Christian Democratic Union party. The MonoKnig bookstore. Ned Garvey MnogoKnig MnogoKnig, the bookstore inside the Russian House facing Friedrichstrasse, has also been accused of being an instrument of Russia’s propaganda apparatus for selling soaps and other products that evoke Russia’s war in Ukraine. Yet the Latvia-based bookstore chain sells books in Russian, Ukrainian, English and other languages, including books banned in Russia such as slain Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny’s “ Patriot ” and journalist Elena Kostyuchenko’s “ I Love Russia .” The store made headlines last week after Latvia’s State Security Service raided four of the chain’s locations in Riga over alleged violations of EU sanctions. “German newspapers accused [MnogoKnig] of selling coloring books featuring a T-34 tank, claiming this was Russian propaganda. But this is so far from the truth,” a source close to the Russian House told The Moscow Times, speaking on condition of anonymity. They added that the store also sells books that are banned in Russia. “As far as propaganda goes, I think if the leadership in Moscow knew about this, they’d be more likely to scold the Russian House in Berlin for not being ‘Z’ enough,” they said, referring to a symbol widely used by pro-war Russians. https://screenrant.com/best-non-disney-a.text: By Sarah Polonsky Published Sep 12, 2026, 6:18 AM EDT Senior Music Editor at Screen Rant , Sarah's love of sound and story drive the beat. A globetrotting brand whisperer and award-winning journalist, she’s built cross-cultural narratives around the world—but music has always been her true north. She launched DJ Mag North America, successfully introducing the iconic UK brand to the U.S. market. Previously, she carved a space for EDM inside the pages of VIBE , blending electronic and hip-hop culture long before it was trendy. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Summary Non-Disney studios and auteurs delivered many of animation's boldest, award-winning films recently. Innovative visual styles, from CG multiverses to painterly and stop-motion, reshaped mainstream animation. Franchises and small films alike found new life by embracing risk, emotion, and distinct artistic voices. Disney and Pixar spent decades setting the standard for mainstream animation, and there are still plenty of Disney movies worth revisiting before their upcoming sequels . However, some of the best animated movies of the last five years have come from elsewhere. DreamWorks and Sony have experimented with striking new visual styles, while filmmakers including Hayao Miyazaki and Guillermo del Toro have shown how much room remains for traditional and stop-motion animation. The Academy Awards tell part of the story. Disney has not won Best Animated Feature since Encanto took the prize in 2022. Since then, Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio , The Boy and the Heron , Flow , and KPop Demon Hunters have won the category in consecutive years. Even as plenty of forgotten Disney movies continue to hold up surprisingly well , some of animation's most exciting recent work has come from outside the studio. Awards only tell part of the story, though. Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse became a blockbuster while pushing CG animation somewhere visually unexpected, and The Wild Robot became one of DreamWorks' most acclaimed recent releases. Others breathed new life into franchises that had already been around for decades. These eight movies are not ranked against each other. Instead, they represent some of the strongest animated films released outside Disney during a particularly exciting five-year stretch. KPop Demon Hunters (2025) Rumi, Zoey and Mira from KPop Demon Hunters KPop Demon Hunters arrived on Netflix in June 2025 and became something much bigger than another animated streaming release. The musical fantasy follows K-pop superstars Rumi, Mira, and Zoey, who balance their lives as HUNTR/X with a secret mission protecting humanity from demons. The movie became Netflix's most popular original title ever and went on to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Its success is easy to understand. The action is energetic, the animation has its own identity, and the songs became hits outside the movie itself. The creators and cast of KPop Demon Hunters clearly tapped into something much bigger than a standard animated musical. The Wild Robot (2024) Roz in The Wild Robot DreamWorks delivered one of its most moving movies in years with The Wild Robot . Adapted from Peter Brown's novel and directed by Chris Sanders, the film follows Roz, a robot stranded on an island who gradually forms relationships with its animals and becomes the surrogate mother of an orphaned gosling named Brightbill. Lupita Nyong'o gives Roz an enormous amount of warmth without losing the character's mechanical origins. Just as memorable is the movie's painterly animation, which makes the natural world feel closer to an illustrated storybook than conventional CG. The Wild Robot earned a Best Animated Feature Oscar nomination and grossed more than $330 million worldwide. Flow (2024) Flow 2024 movie There is no dialogue in Flow , and it doesn't need any. Latvian filmmaker Gints Zilbalodis follows a solitary black cat whose home is destroyed by a massive flood. The cat boards a small boat with other animals, forcing creatures that would ordinarily avoid one another to survive together as the water continues to rise. That simple premise becomes surprisingly emotional without relying on human voices or familiar animated-movie formulas. Flow also became a remarkable awards success, winning Best Animated Feature at the 2025 Academy Awards. Its comparatively small scale makes the accomplishment even more impressive beside the massive studio productions that usually dominate the category. Spider-Man: Across The Spider-Verse (2023) Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse had already changed expectations for mainstream CG animation, which left its sequel with an enormous challenge. Across the Spider-Verse somehow became even more visually ambitious, sending Miles Morales through different dimensions that each possess their own distinctive animation styles . It is also much more than a technical showcase. Miles' conflict with Miguel O'Hara gives the movie an emotional argument about whether being Spider-Man requires accepting tragedy as inevitable. Audiences responded in a huge way: Across the Spider-Verse earned more than $690 million worldwide and received an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature. The Boy And The Heron (2023) One-Piece-The-Boy-And-The-Heron-Weathering-With-You-Feature-Header Image By Joshua Fox Hayao Miyazaki returned with The Boy and the Heron , his first feature in a decade and one of Studio Ghibli's most visually extraordinary movies. Set during World War II, it centers on Mahito, a grieving boy who follows a mysterious gray heron into a strange world after moving to the countryside with his father. Like many Miyazaki films, explaining the plot only gets someone so far. The movie moves between grief and fantasy with dreamlike logic, allowing Mahito's journey to become increasingly surreal. Its place among the best anime movies of the 2020s was cemented when The Boy and the Heron won Best Animated Feature at the 2024 Academy Awards. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem (2023) The Turtles in fighting stances in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles have been rebooted so many times that another animated version could easily have felt unnecessary. Instead, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem found a reason to start over by emphasizing something surprisingly easy to forget about Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo, and Donatello: they are teenagers. Actual teenage actors voice the four brothers, giving their conversations an appropriately messy energy. The movie's sketch-like animation makes it stand apart from earlier TMNT adaptations, while its story lets the turtles behave like kids who desperately want friends and normal lives. It is one of the rare franchise reboots that immediately establishes its own personality. Puss In Boots: The Last Wish (2022) Puss in Boots in The Last Wish Few expected a sequel arriving 11 years after Puss in Boots to become one of DreamWorks' best movies. Puss in Boots: The Last Wish begins with the famously fearless hero discovering that he has burned through eight of his nine lives, turning his latest adventure into an unexpectedly thoughtful story about mortality. Like many family movies secretly made for adults , it gives younger viewers a colorful adventure while confronting something much heavier underneath. Its stylized action also gave the Shrek franchise a visual overhaul, helping The Last Wish earn more than $480 million worldwide and a Best Animated Feature Oscar nomination. Guillermo Del Toro's Pinocchio (2022) A man and a wooden puppet in Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio. The same year Disney released its live-action Pinocchio remake, Guillermo del Toro offered a radically different interpretation of Carlo Collodi's familiar story. His stop-motion version relocates much of the action to Fascist Italy and approaches Pinocchio's creation through the grief of Geppetto, who has lost his human son. The result is darker than most family adaptations of Pinocchio , but never needlessly grim. Del Toro uses the story to explore death, disobedience, and what makes a life meaningful, while the painstaking stop-motion work gives every character a physical presence. The movie won the 2023 Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, beginning four consecutive non-Disney victories in the category. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/28/at-l.text: At least 81 people have been killed after days of heavy rain and flooding in northern India’s Uttar Pradesh state, officials said on Monday.The state government said 46 people were injured and more than 1,000 houses were damaged after three days of heavy rainfall caused flooding in several districts.Schools were closed in parts of the state on Monday, including the capital Lucknow, while rescue teams moved people from flooded areas to safer locations.Residents were advised to avoid unnecessary travel through waterlogged areas and stay away from fast-flowing rivers, streams and drains.Rainfall was expected to ease from Monday as a weather system over the Bay of Bengal weakened, said Atul Kumar Singh, a senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow.Light rain could continue in eastern and western parts of the state through Tuesday, he said.Flooding also affected the eastern state of Odisha, where more than 75,000 people were evacuated to safer areas, officials said.In neighbouring Nepal, 21 people died in weather-related incidents between Thursday and Sunday, the country's disaster management agency said.Five people remained missing and five others were injured, while floods and landslides damaged 194 houses.Nepal is recovering from devastating August floods that killed more than 1,400 people and left nearly 6,000 missing.

https://www.politico.eu/article/albania-.text: TIRANA, Albania — Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama took a playful shot at U.S. Democrats over ongoing “ Flamingo Revolution ” protests against a planned luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law. What started as protests against the project has evolved into broader anti-government protests and is now entering its 124th consecutive day, drawing widespread international media attention. Rama attributed this attention to the “long shadow of Donald Trump,” in an interview with WELT, which, like POLITICO, is part of Axel Springer’s Global Reporters Network. Advertisement Advertisement He added: “I told my Democratic friends in America: If you cannot beat Trump in America, do not come to Albania to take revenge. That is not fair.” Kushner is linked to a multi-billion-dollar project to develop a luxury resort on the uninhabited southern Albanian island of Sazan and an adjacent strip of shoreline next to a protected area inhabited by flamingos, pelicans and diverse wetland wildlife. The plans sparked national and international protests at the end of May, with rallies ongoing every night outside Rama’s office in Tirana. The protests drew widespread attention, with a resolution in the European Parliament, and international clothing brand Patagonia , and Kosovo-Albanian pop singer Dua Lipa getting involved. Rama said the plans involve two projects: One on the publicly owned Sazan Island, a former Soviet military base, with only 8% to be developed, and another on a privately owned peninsula. Protestors object to the project over environmental concerns and a lack of public consultation. Meanwhile, the country’s EU- and U.S.-backed Special Prosecutor’s Office for Organized Crime and Corruption, SPAK, is investigating whether an Albanian businessman faked ownership documents related to the private land. The former owner has denied any wrongdoing. A spokesperson for the project’s investors, including Kushner, did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication. Advertisement Advertisement Objecting to protest slogans such as “Albania is not for sale” and “Albania for Albanians”, Rama said, “If you were bringing foreign capital into Germany, would you then say that Germany was being sold off?” “I represent the interests of my country, and I will continue to do so,” he added. He also said negotiations over the project were still ongoing and that they would assess its environmental impact. At a press conference in Tirana Wednesday with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Rama assured that his government will “shine a spotlight on the process by ensuring full transparency regarding all documents related to this widely discussed project.” While Rama met the EU Commission chief, several hundred people protested outside his office with placards reading “No EU with Rama.” The Axel Springer Global Reporters Network harnesses the resources of the company’s newsrooms to publish ambitious scoops, investigations, interviews, opinion pieces and analysis. It allows journalists — including those from POLITICO, Business Insider, WELT, BILD, Onet and Fakt — to collaborate on major stories for an international audience of hundreds of millions across platforms: online, print, TV and audio. https://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/news.text: Crimestoppers Court Crime Crimestoppers' most wanted list in London - rapist to murder probe Crimestoppers Court Crime By Josh Bolton Court and crime reporter Share 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A convicted rapist and a man linked to a homicide investigation are among the Londoners on the Crimestoppers most wanted list. The Crimestoppers charity collates appeals and information from police forces across the country. As of September 2026, these are the wanted men and women who police believe may be in London. If you see these individuals do not approach them, call Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or call police on 101. Shasho Mohammedi Shasho Mohammedi (Image: Crimestoppers) Sasho Mohammedi is wanted on recall to prison having been released from HMP Belmarsh in south east London. He has links to Hounslow, as well as various other areas in the UK including Bolton, Slough, Fleetwood, Leicestershire and Portsmouth. He has also been known to go by Sware Hame, Shaho Mohammadi and Lala. Liam Byron Liam Byron (Image: Crimestoppers) Liam Byron is wanted on a recall to prison issued on August 15, 2024. He was originally in prison for possession with intent to supply class A drugs. Crimestoppers said he is thin, around 5ft4 tall and has short cropped hair. Alexandru Oprea Alexandru Oprea (Image: Crimestoppers) Alexandru Oprea is wanted for rape. He was sentenced to more than 11 years in prison for rape, sexual assaults, indecent exposure and other offences in June after he failed to attend his trial. The offences were committed in Essex in 2023. Oprea has links to London, Leicester and Romania. He has sleeve style tattoos on both arms, on his chest and his stomach. His victim said: "I have waited three years for this moment, I am praying every day that he will be found as soon as possible, people like him do not deserve to be free with no consequences. "I am still struggling to calm myself because after the sentencing it feels like everything is coming back to my mind. "I am extremely grateful for all the support." Pierre Thompson Officers are now looking to speak to 41-year-old Pierre Thompson (pictured). (Image: MPS) Police are searching for Pierre Thompson, 41, from west London, as part of their enquiries into a murder. Simon Whyte, 55, died after being shot on Harrow Road in Stonebridge, at approximately 9.35pm on December 19, 2025. Detective Inspector Jim Barry, who is leading the investigation, said: "Today marks six months since Simon’s death and his family and friends are continuing to come to terms with their loss. "They are desperate for answers as to what happened that evening and we have already carried out extensive enquiries to build up a picture of the events of that night. "We are now appealing to the public to help us progress our investigation and would urge anyone who knows the whereabouts of Pierre Thompson to contact police or independent charity Crimestoppers immediately." Fabian Maxwell Fabion Maxwell (Image: Crimestoppers) Fabian Maxwell is wanted on recall to prison. He has links to Burgess Hill, Lewisham and Bromley. Yuxuan Yang Yuxuan Yang (Image: Crimestoppers) Yuxuan Yang, also known as Owen, is wanted for failing to appear at a magistrates court in North Wales. He had been charged with meeting a girl under 16 following grooming, sexual activity with a female under 16, causing of inciting a female under 16 to engaged in sexual activity and making indecent photographs of children. Yang, aged in his late 20s, previously resided in central London. He is approximately 5ft10, slim and has black hair. Rayan Mayou Rayan Mayou (Image: Newsquest) Rayan Mayou, who may also go by Jacob Janvier, is wanted on suspicion of robbing a high value watch. The alleged the victim had their watch stolen at Regents Park Underground Station by two individuals. Mayou's last known address was in Croydon. He is in his early 20s. Adam Bucholc Adam Bucholc (Image: Crimestoppers) Adam Bucholc is wanted in relation to extradition proceedings. He is believed to frequent the Haringey area. He wears glasses and has a tattoo on his left arm and hand. Reece Westley Jillings Reece Westley Jillings (Image: Crimestoppers) Reece Westley Jillings is wanted on suspicion of conspiracy to import and supply cocaine. It relates to a Met Police investigation named Operation Detox. Jillings is in his 40s, approximately 5ft8 tall and has a "croaky London accent". Beauty Chikonzelo Chaima Beauty Chikonzelo Chaima (Image: Crimestoppers) Beauty Chikonzelo Chaima is wanted on suspicion of illegal immigration offences at Heathrow Airport. She is suspected of attempting to facilitate three people arriving from Ethiopia. She may be in London or the East Midlands. Muhammed Babar Bashir Muhammed Babar Bashir (Image: Crimestoppers) Muhammed Babar Bashir, originally from Pakistan, is wanted on suspicion of illegal immigration offences. A warrant was issued by Manchester Crown Court on January 29, 2019. He may be in London, Manchester, Lancashire or Yorkshire. https://www.politico.eu/article/former-b.text: BRUSSELS — Former Belgian Prime Minister Guy Verhofstadt is under investigation by Belgian federal prosecutors over the supervision of European Parliament interns during his time as leader of the liberal group. The investigation, which was first reported by Belgian magazine Knack , apparently began this year. It focuses on the period from 2009 to 2019 when Verhofstadt chaired the Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe group in the Parliament. ALDE was succeeded by Renew Europe after the 2019 European election. An EU official familiar with the matter, who was granted anonymity to speak freely, confirmed to POLITICO that Verhofstadt is under investigation for the way in which he supervised parliamentary interns. They said the probe was initiated by the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO), but is now being conducted by Belgian authorities on behalf of the EU bodies. Advertisement Advertisement “OLAF has merely requested information from our client regarding the supervision of a number of interns … in which he, as group chair, was not personally involved,” lawyers Christine Mussche and Quinten De Keersmaecker, who are representing Verhofstadt in the case, told Knack. “Verhofstadt himself has not yet been interviewed, and there are currently no specific allegations against him. He is cooperating fully with OLAF and has provided the requested explanations with complete transparency,” the lawyers added. Reached by POLITICO, Verhofstadt declined to comment further. In a written reply Sunday, EPPO spokesperson Tine Hollevoet said: “As a general rule, the EPPO does not comment on ongoing investigations, nor do we publicly confirm which cases we are working on, in order not to endanger the possible ongoing procedures and their outcome.” The Belgian Federal Prosecutor’s Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Verhofstadt, who was Belgium’s prime minister from 1999 to 2008 and served as an MEP from 2009 to 2024, is a prominent pro-EU figure who represented the European Parliament in the Brexit negotiations following the U.K.’s 2016 referendum on EU membership. He left the Parliament in 2024 and is currently president of the board of the European Movement International , a pro-Europe lobby. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.energy-pedia.com/news/poland.text: Daily Newsletter Advertise Contact Home Latest news News categories Exploration Development/Production Licensing Seismic Alternative Energy General Regional news European/Caspian/CIS Central SE Asia/Australasia South America/Gulf of Mexico Middle East /Africa News archives energy-pedia opportunities energy-pedia jobs Events energy-pedia alternative energy Europe / Caspian / CIS >>>Â Poland Poland: Greenvolt and Statkraft sign agreement for the management of 400 MW of battery storage in Poland 30 Sep 2026 10-year agreement structured as a tolling arrangement, giving Statkraft commercial management of the batteries across energy and flexibility markets. Covers the Elk and Turosn Koscielna projects in Poland, each with 200 MW / 800 MWh of capacity. The largest publicly communicated BESS agreement of its kind in the European Union to date. Statkraft , Europe’s largest producer of renewable energy and a leading PPA provider in Europe, and Greenvolt Power , a global utility-scale developer of onshore wind, solar and battery storage projects, have signed a 10-year tolling agreement covering 400 MW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across two projects in Poland. The agreement is the largest publicly communicated in the EU to date* and marks Statkraft's first large-scale BESS contract in the Polish market. The agreement covers two four-hour batteries, Elk (200 MW/800 MWh) and Turosn Koscielna (200 MW/800 MWh), located in Nowa Wies Elcka and Turosn Koscielna respectively . The structure of a tolling agreement gives Statkraft the right to decide when the batteries charge and discharge across energy and flexibility markets, while giving Greenvolt an additional source of predictable, long-term revenue alongside the revenue already secured through Poland’s Capacity Market. 'Our partnership with Greenvolt shows our ambition in Poland. With the largest BESS transaction signed in the country to date, we continue to play an active role in supporting Poland’s energy transition. The two BESS projects complement our portfolio of third-party wind and solar assets, on the back of which we can offer competitive and stable prices for energy-intensive off-takers. Having previously signed Poland's largest cPPA and first subsidy-free utility-based solar PPA, we are proud to add another landmark transaction,' says Kornel Koronowski, Head of Origination Poland, Statkraft. 'This agreement with Statkraft brings sophisticated market optimisation to these projects, allowing the flexibility of the batteries to be monetised across different power markets and unlocking additional revenues. We have built strong capabilities in originating and developing utility-scale assets and, as we move further along the value chain, with projects now entering operation, choosing the right commercial structure is increasingly important', says Lukasz Zagórski, Business Origination and Market Regulation Director, Greenvolt Power. As Poland's power system incorporates increasing amounts of renewable energy, battery energy storage systems are expected to play an increasingly important role. By storing surplus renewable electricity and releasing it when demand is higher, utility-scale batteries help balance supply and demand, stabilise the grid and facilitate the integration of more wind and solar power into Poland’s energy mix. The partnership combines Greenvolt's expertise in developing large-scale energy assets with Statkraft's ability to manage electricity market risk . Through long-term tolling agreements, projects benefit from greater revenue certainty, supporting financing and accelerating the deployment of battery storage infrastructure at scale. This partnership demonstrates the growing maturity of Poland's flexibility market and the importance of innovative commercial structures in enabling new energy infrastructure. *The largest publicly communicated BESS agreement in the European Union at the date of publication Source: Greenvolt A global information service for upstream oil and gas opportunities - divestitures, farmins and farmouts and licensing rounds.
